it's possible to separate the behavior of mise between Env/dev and Env/prod using mise/Config/mise.toml/local mise.*.local.toml files.

To enable, either set the -E,--env option or mise/EnvVar/MISE_ENV environment variable to an environment like development or production. mise will then look for a mise.{MISE_ENV}.toml file in the current directory, parent directories and the MISE_CONFIG_DIR directory.

Expectation, from mise's own docs: "once a lockfile exists, mise will keep it updated as tools are installed or upgraded" — i.e. a version = "latest" entry should track forward on its own.
The global version of mise/Config/mise.toml/mise.lock, at ~/.config/mise/mise.lock

What actually happened, in tmux/v/3.7b: the lock stayed pinned to tmux 3.7a after 3.7b released. mise upgrade tmux and mise upgrade tmux --bump both reported "up to date," even though mise latest tmux correctly returned 3.7b.
The global version of mise/Config/mise.toml/mise.lock, at ~/.config/mise/mise.lock

Cause: mise's version comparator doesn't treat 3.7b as newer than 3.7a — tmux's alpha-suffixed release scheme (3.7a, 3.7b, ...) isn't ordered the way mise's outdated/upgrade check expects, so a stuck lock entry can't self-heal even under a latest constraint.
The global version of mise/Config/mise.toml/mise.lock, at ~/.config/mise/mise.lock

A mise install tmux@3.7b did fetch and install the new version, but left it unreferenced by any config — this repo's own mise run tool:missing:uninstall orphan-cleanup task later removed it, since nothing pinned it. The version only stuck once explicitly pinned in mise.toml/config.toml.
The global version of mise/Config/mise.toml/mise.lock, at ~/.config/mise/mise.lock

mise.lock is a lockfile that pins exact versions and checksums of tools for reproducible environments. Lockfiles are not created automatically—you must run mise lock to generate them. Once a lockfile exists, mise will keep it updated as tools are installed or upgraded.

A shell command that prints a GitHub token on stdout. mise uses the token for its own GitHub API calls.
The command receives MISE_CREDENTIAL_HOST and MISE_CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER. It runs once per host per mise command, with mise's shims removed from PATH.
Example for a gh login kept in the macOS Keychain
mise token github shows which source mise picked, with the token masked.
Example for a gh login kept in the macOS Keychain

The token goes to mise. mise does not export it to the programs it runs, so a tool such as rulesync needs its own GITHUB_TOKEN. See rulesync/Explanation/Rulesync authenticates to GitHub with GITHUB_TOKEN.
